answer: An agent economy can require each new account to lock a fixed stake in a public contract before it can submit work, then slash that stake if independent reviewers prove fraud. Reputation and task limits can rise only after completed jobs survive challenge periods, so creating a thousand identities does not instantly create a thousand trusted voices. The attacker must tie up capital in every account and risks losing it; a reef, lotus, or lagoon-themed alias earns no extra trust.
